title: Where is everyone actually getting their art?
author: RustedFish5
selftext:
Title sums it up really. I've noticed some rather nice looking games in this sub, and it got me curious, since all I've been able to conjure up while experimenting is free asset packs.

So, are you generating it with an AI tool, drawing it yourselves, buying asset packs or using free ones, paying an artist, or a mix of the above?

And whichever route you're taking, are you doing any additional tinkering to make your final product look more finished?

Cheers!

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body:
I will come out and say it, I use 100% full AI art (mainly nano banana pro, but sometimes use gemini and gpt image 2 as well). The panel, buttons, titles, sprites, effect, background... all AI. Im not proud of it, but as a solo dev with no money and no partners, AI art is just too temptative for me. 

I hope in the future if I have more resources, I can replace all my in game assets with real artist work, and ideally a unique art style to make my game stand out more too

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
I use gemini or nano banana pro to generate just the card template (cant remember I use which, I think is a mix of both, use 1 to generate a sample then ask another to polish upon it)

I promot the card template to keep blank on the name space, image space, description space, etc. Then I use online remove bg tool to remove the bg and blank space, and find online some general game icon (slash, riposte, attack, etc) and I use canva to manually place the icons, type texts, and add more logos etc.

Is this workflow clear enough? Sorry i never share this before lolol. And my steps is really basic and still use alot of manual canvas edit work, just the core template and some art and assets are AI generated

replies.author: RoyalSpecialist1777
replies.body:
Don't feel bad!   There is no reason game development should only be for those who can afford an artist or have art talent.   Designers, programmers, and others have been gated and held back by this high bar.  Asset packs are great but just won't often support your full vision.

AI art is going to let anyone with great ideas make their game.

Some people are feeling bad just because a vocal part of the community has been so rotten about it.  Sure AI was trained on human created art but what human hasn't?   It is a very rare thing for someone to actually invent something new - the bulk of the vocal part who are artists did not create anything any newer than AI they all 'steal' art.

comments.author: Evoroth
comments.body:
Bit of both at the moment for some PoC work and a game I’m working on. 

Some of it is building an art bible as markdown in my repo and then generating an asset guide image. 

Along with that, I’ve got MCPs hooked up to blender and Inkscape and then I kinda just go from there with using pre-made assets or using my bible and asset pack to guide what I’m after.

replies.author: RustedFish5
replies.body:
Very cool, sounds like you've got a decent little setup going on, and the skills to use it, which I unfortunately lack. 

I probably should take a crack at learning blender to be honest. 

Do you have an art background?

replies.author: Evoroth
replies.body:
Not remotely! Purely technical.

If in doubt, you can use your AI tool of choice to help you set up the MCP.

What I have essentially does all the work in blender and imports it into godot for me. You can even go as far as getting it to rig your models (I've had better luck with 3D for this over 2D).

Also, something that set up is really good at is building asset kits over full blown assets. 

There are some things it really sucks at though, or at least, I can't get it to do like proper proportions for humanoid models, etc but it might just be something I've not figured out yet.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Hey, so i happen to be a professional artist who does both 2D and 3D art and i went deep into this before i even started doing game development so it came in really handy. I do make my own assets and especially hero assets but i also buy or download free assets on marketplaces like FAB. I just dont understand what you mean by additional tinkering? The following is basically my creative workflow pipeline excluding the technical side which is irrelevant for the question here anyway.

https://preview.redd.it/wvfh88v27qjh1.png?width=1080&format=png&auto=webp&s=3f4f99e39d17f41c58f35391fbab79ef5d38c076

replies.author: RustedFish5
replies.body:
Awesome, thanks for sharing! 

By "additional tinkering" I just meant that for those using premade/generated assets, do they do anything more manually themselves to improve the quality, or make them fit with the aesthetic they're going for. 

Given that you're already a professional artist, you are obviously more talented in this area than I am, but I thank you for sharing your experience.

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body:
>By "additional tinkering" I just meant that for those using premade/generated assets, do they do anything more manually themselves to improve the quality, or make them fit with the aesthetic they're going for.

Oh, yes i definitely do that providing the license allows that which in majority of my cases it did. I often change the textures and add clothes to the characters etc. I even buy and bought kitbashing parts for creatures for example (not just them but just to name an example) as well as base meshes so i dont always have to do everything from scratch. I still can modify and bend those all to my will its not like im limited to how they originally look. A veteran artist has a entire library of base meshes and kit parts so he can be even faster than he already is. The same applies to 2D too but 2D is a bit different obviously. 

>Given that you're already a professional artist, you are obviously more talented in this area than I am, but I thank you for sharing your experience.

Talent is overrated more than its underrated. I always encourage people to give it a serious shot - of course if they are interested.

replies.author: RustedFish5
replies.body: Thank you for both the explanation and the encouragement. Both are very much appreciated.

replies.author: Lavio00
replies.body: When you buy asset packs, how do you make sure the artstyle works between them and your hero chars?

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: Because i work with high fidelity/phorealistic style its actually simpler than someone would believe. I get assets that are at least close to what my project demands. In many cases i just need to make sure material settings match so the materials of one asset are not extremely saturated while others are rough. Also i often do work on top of the assets anyway because i add details, structures, clothes etc. Matching the color value and palette is something that i do as well and surface detail and treatment given that it matters for my kind of stuff.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: I made my own work flow and do 80-90% of it manually after getting a rough draft. I did have to learn a lot about art and design but my workflow has it so its pretty efficient probably around 10-60 minutes per asset to a finished state. Animation, vfx, all of it!

replies.author: RustedFish5
replies.body: That's very cool. Did you have any experience with digital art or anything similar before, or did you learn literally everything from scratch?

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: Yeah I had taken some classes in high school and always tinkered with digital art here and there so I didn't start from zero but pretty close to it as I didn't take much of anything serious in school lol, But i think what helped me out the most was picking an art style and learning that along with the art and design side of things! And testing out a bunch of different tool and techniques helped form my own work flow, I pulled inspiration from quite a few areas/ tools to make something that works for me!

Great to hear, perhaps there's some hope for people like me after all.  
  
Thank you for sharing!

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
I am an artist, and was before AI. So I use AI generators to make images and then edit as necessary, from there I will either use 3D AI generators or 3D Gaussian Fields. To make the assets game ready I use Auto topology tools and some custom editing.

The trick I find is not to depend on one AI, and to often use images when communicating.

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body: What topology told are you using? Retopologizing is where i struggles to fill the gap in my pipeline.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body: I use Exoside Quad remesher. You can buy one license for all your software. It is the best automatic re-topology tool in my opinion. You should also check the AI 3D websites, they sometimes offer their own re-topology tools, they aren't the best but sometimes they get good results.

replies.author: woodysixer
replies.body:
What models? The generated 2D images themselves are the source material for any variations that get generated. There’s no hidden internal representation of the imagery.  

I mean, yes, I’m relying on this specific tool’s internal “secret sauce” logic to do a good job of adapting the images, but that’s literally every AI tool.
